newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, Jan gains on weather.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, Jan gains on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a moderate session, with January sinking early on Wednesday's bearish AGA report but edging up later on forecasts for colder weather next week, sources said.
January gained 3.6 cents to close at $3.529 per million British thermal units. February settled 2.7 cents lower at $3.212. Other deferreds ended narrowly mixed.

"People were riding the weather report. Colder temps may continue to carry the front of the board, but the back is not following, which could mean the market is not embracing a longer-term bullish scenario," said one Midwest trader.
Most agreed 6-10 day forecasts calling for below-normal temperatures for much of the nation helped prop up nearby futures today.
But some expected concerns about low storage to wane in coming weeks, as weekly declines fail to match last December's weekly average drawdown of 142 bcf.
"It's possible that the year-on-year gap will be closed by January 1," the Midwest trader said, referring to current stocks at 214 bcf, or eight percent, below last year.

Traders said prices also rallied early on news one of three 30-inch TransCanada lines ruptured late Wednesday in western Ontario, but slid later when the company said no deliveries were affected because it was able to re-route gas.

Technical traders said the market was range-bound, with support in January still in the $3.19 area, then $3.11 and $3.04. Resistance was seen in the mid-$3.50s and then at $3.70. Major resistance was pegged at the $3.80 contract high.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices were talked down slightly Thursday at about the $3.40 level. Midcontinent pipes also were slightly lower in the low-$3.30s. New York city gate gas was talked a couple of cents lower at about $4.00.
The 12-month strip edged up 0.3 cent to $3.505. NYMEX said 36,779 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 45,523.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was untraded, but January finished two cents higher at $1.65.
NYMEX Permian natgas also did not trade. January settled unchanged at $3.25.
On the KCBT, January ended 8.5 cents higher at $3.43, while deferreds closed up by three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.9 cents to 9.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
